decisions.decision: CLI for human approval instead of JSON editing
decisions.rationale: CLI commands are auditable (command history), idempotent (re-running approve is safe), and prevent JSON syntax errors. Each command is loggable as evidence in the audit trail.

decisions.decision: Confidence < 0.7 hard floor always requires human approval
decisions.rationale: Auditors need a guarantee that auto-promote cannot bypass risky matches. The REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL toggle is a convenience for dev/demo — the hard floor is a safety net that cannot be disabled without code changes.
alternatives_considered: No auto-promote at all (too restrictive for known entities)

decisions.rationale: Same pattern as raw zone. Single catalog DB, different namespaces (raw, base). DuckDB can query across namespaces in one connection.
Mirrors raw zone pattern (data/raw/iceberg_warehouse). Zone separation at the filesystem level makes it clear which zone owns which data files.

decisions.decision: Archive staging files with timestamp instead of deleting
decisions.rationale: Preserves the full proposal history without requiring Iceberg time-travel queries. Archived files are cheap storage and valuable for auditing.

decisions.decision: Rejected mappings stay out of entity_mappings table
decisions.rationale: Downstream consumers query WHERE status = 'approved' — rejected entries would be noise. Full rejection history is in entity_resolution_audit where auditors look for it.
alternatives_considered: Include rejected in entity_mappings with status filter (adds noise)

decisions.decision: Two audit entries per approved mapping (proposed + approved)
decisions.rationale: Each state transition is a separate audit entry with its own timestamp and actor. This captures the full lifecycle: who proposed, who approved, when each happened.
Core resolution logic is testable without an Iceberg table. resolve_entities_from_records takes raw dicts, resolve_entities reads from Iceberg. Same algorithm, different data source.

decisions.decision: Only archive staging when no pending proposals remain
decisions.rationale: If a partial approve is done (e.g., approve ER-001 but not ER-002), the staging file must persist so ER-002 can still be reviewed. Archive only when all proposals are resolved.
decisions.discovery: Initial implementation archived after any promote, which broke partial approvals. Fixed to check for remaining pending proposals before archiving.
